note: the customer with five open jobs is returned above the one with a single open job, every time.
evidence:
Run on the test branch on 18 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209, watched on screen and read from the product's own answer.

Typed ZZOPENCOUNT and opened the Customers list:
  1. ZZOPENCOUNT Freight Busy   - badge reads '5 open'
  2. ZZOPENCOUNT Freight Quiet  - badge reads '1 open'

The two records are the same in every other way - same address, same style of name, both found through the same field - so the number of open jobs is the only thing that can separate them, and it puts the busier one first.

READ FOUR TIMES IN A ROW, always in the same order, so this is not chance. A control was read alongside it: a pair with no open jobs at all comes back in a stable order of its own, which shows the list is not simply shuffling.

ONE HONEST LIMIT: both rows carry the product's top score, so the number itself cannot show the size of the lift - the order is the evidence, not the score. The requirement asks for the busier customer to rank higher, and it does.

note: a customer found by its own name is returned above one found only by its street address.
evidence:
Run on the test branch on 18 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209, watched on screen and read from the product's own answer.

Typed ZZNAMEBONUS and opened the Customers list:
  1. ZZNAMEBONUS Cartage        - the words are in the company NAME
  2. Sterling Brothers Freight  - the words are only in its ADDRESS (40 ZZNAMEBONUS Road)

The product's own numbers show why, and they match the requirement exactly: the name match scores 0.80 and the address match 0.70 - a gap of 0.10, which is the bonus the requirement gives to a match on the name over a match on any other field. Neither customer has any open jobs, so nothing else is lifting either one.

note: typing the exact number of a work order you are not allowed to see returns nothing at all - it is not pinned at the top and not in any list.
evidence:
Run on the test branch on 18 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209.

FIRST THE CONTROL, as a full-access user: typing S2-15430 returns exactly one result, the work order itself, shown at the top. So the record exists and is findable.

THEN AS A PERSON WITHOUT WORK ORDER ACCESS (the role was assigned through the staff screen and read back before searching): typing the same number returns NOTHING - every heading reads zero, and the Work orders heading is not even offered. The record is not pinned at the top either.

An exact number is the strongest kind of match there is, so this is the case most likely to slip past a permission check. It does not.

note: a person missing two whole areas loses all four affected lists together, and everything else comes back exactly as before.
evidence:
Run on the test branch on 18 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209.

FIRST THE CONTROL, as a full-access user: typing 'Fib' returns all eight kinds of record - work orders 20, customers 3, vehicles 6, parts 4, suppliers 1, part sales 1, purchase orders 6, supplier invoices 4.

THEN AS A PERSON MISSING BOTH WORK ORDERS AND SUPPLIER ORDERING (this role exists on the branch already - it is the one the handover asked me to confirm; role assigned and read back first): the same search returns customers 3, vehicles 6, parts 4, part sales 1 - the same counts as before - and work orders, suppliers, purchase orders and supplier invoices are gone completely. Not shown as empty: no heading, no count, no tab for any of the four.

That is the point of the check: several areas disappear together and cleanly, and nothing the person IS allowed to see is affected.

note: a misspelled search does not surface a part from someone who cannot see parts.
evidence:
Run on the test branch on 18 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209.

FIRST THE CONTROL, as a full-access user: typing 'Altenator', a misspelling of Alternator, returns six parts, each marked as a close match. So the misspelling does reach those parts.

THEN AS A PERSON WITHOUT PARTS ACCESS (role assigned and read back first): the same misspelling returns no parts at all and the Parts heading is not offered. Access is applied to near-miss matches as well as exact ones, which is what this check is for.

WORTH KNOWING, NOT A FAULT: that person still sees purchase orders, which they are allowed to see, and those lines say they matched on a part name. The requirement lists part names on a purchase order as part of the purchase order's own searchable text, so this is the product behaving as written, not the parts list leaking.
